cards.title: AI supplier scout sourcing report sequence
cards.claim: In this walkthrough, the White Labeler AI supplier scout version two produces a product identity card and a sourcing report covering suppliers, costs, margins, selling approach, and a verdict; the reported verdict is to start with drop shipping, then after orders use Zenrop or Spocket for faster delivery, and after more sales move into private labeling.
cards.action: When sourcing with this AI employee, load the employee, paste it into Claude, upload a captured page screenshot if desired, then review the generated product identity card and sourcing report for supplier costs, margins, selling approach, and verdict.
applies_when: when using White Labeler AI supplier scout version two for product sourcing
when you have product details already established in the Claude workspace
when you can optionally provide a captured screenshot of the product page
do_not_use_when: when you need verified supplier pricing, terms, or compliance details before making decisions
when the product is not suitable for drop shipping, Zenrop/Spocket, or private labeling
unknowns: whether the drop-shipping-to-private-label sequence applies beyond the described product
evidence_quotes: we use the white labeler AI supplier scout version two
Then it does a product identity card
and then it does a sourcing report
what are the costs and the margins associated
move to Zenrop or Spocket for uh faster delivery

cards.title: Drop shipping with branding-visible website when inventory budget is limited
cards.claim: If you cannot spend even $500 to $1,000 on inventory plus branding and packaging, the passage recommends drop shipping and using the drop shipper's supplier images, while keeping your branding visible on the website rather than on product pages to avoid a mismatch between the product customers receive and the one they see; once you have money, switch to branding.
cards.action: For a limited budget, drop ship and use the drop shipping supplier's images to create brand images; keep branding visible on the website, not on product pages; later, when funds allow, switch all over to the branding.
applies_when: when you do not have the ability to spend $500 to $1,000 on inventory and branding/packaging
when you are starting with drop shipping before private labeling
do_not_use_when: when you can already fund inventory and custom branded packaging
when product-page imagery must exactly match the shipped product
unknowns: whether this branding placement affects conversion
the exact budget threshold beyond the stated $500 to $1,000 example
evidence_quotes: If you don't have the ability right now to spend a little bit on getting a little bit of inventory in place, even $500 to $1,000
then go and drop ship it and use this supplier, your drop shipping suppliers images to create all of the images for your brand
the branding that you've done, um, that should be very visible on the website, not on the product pages
once you have the ability and the money then switch all over to the branding

cards.title: Mirror a proven page for a brand with White Labeler
cards.claim: White Labeler takes a proven page and mirrors it for your brand through a four-step process: mirror the page, rebrand it, upgrade it by identifying weaknesses and building missing sections, and launch on Shopify; mirroring requires an account and signed-in state, and the page must be set as either a page where people buy or a page where they do not buy.
cards.action: Use the White Labeler extension's mirror page function on a target page, name the product, decide whether people buy on the page, then follow the mirror, rebrand, upgrade, and Shopify launch steps.
applies_when: when building a Shopify page based on a proven page
when you have a White Labeler account and are signed in
when you can decide whether the page includes checkout/buying
do_not_use_when: when you cannot use White Labeler or Shopify
when you need to avoid copying a proven page's structure or weaknesses
unknowns: whether the mirrored page will reproduce the original page's six- to seven-figure performance
how the upgrade step identifies weaknesses
Shopify page-builder limitations referenced in the passage

there's a four-step process. First, we mirror a page
Then we're going to upgrade the page
and then we launch on Shopify

you're going to need to choose, do people buy on this page or no?
